changelog:
v3.7.0 — Single-Engine Playback (libVLC Removed)

Under the hood
• The app now runs entirely on a single playback engine. The compatible-mode backup engine is gone — its software video decoder is replaced by an FFmpeg-powered fallback built into the main player. Everything from live TV to MKVs to HEVC content plays through one pipeline now, with one set of controls and one caption path.
• Smaller, faster, simpler. APK size drops from ~55MB to ~19MB. No more engine-swap wait when a codec is tricky. No more dual-backend caption quirks.
• 4K hardware HEVC now used on Fire TV Stick 4K Max. A legacy setting was forcing these devices to use software HEVC — turns out your device can handle 4K natively. Fixed.

UX fixes
• Buttons on the binge countdown, end-of-movie, and end-of-series overlays are now actually clickable. Previously the OK press would just show controls without hitting the button.
• Subtitle system unchanged — everything from v3.6.8 carries over and now runs on the simpler single-engine path.
• Frame-rate reporting in diagnostics no longer shows impossible negative values after stream format changes.

Dependencies
• Media3 1.9.0 → 1.10.0
• Jellyfin FFmpeg audio extension → our own combined FFmpeg audio+video extension (h264, hevc, vp9, mpeg2video, vc1, mpeg4 + all audio codecs)
• libVLC removed
